Set up a 2D dam-break simulation using OpenFOAM's interFoam solver with a sharp VOF free surface.
The overall computational domain is 1.0 m long, 0.7 m high, and extruded one cell in the z-direction with a thickness of 0.01 m.
The front and back patch faces in the z-direction are set to boundary type empty, enforcing a true 2D configuration.
The mesh is a uniform structured grid of 100 cells in x, 70 cells in y, and 1 cell in z, generated via blockMeshDict.
The water column is placed flush against the left wall, spanning x from 0 to 0.116 m and the full height y from 0 to 0.7 m.
Initialize the field using setFields so that alpha.water equals 1 inside the rectangular box (0, 0, 0) to (0.116, 0.7, 0.01) and 0 everywhere else.
The setFieldsDict box coordinates must match the blockMeshDict geometry exactly with no deviation in the 0.116 m width or 0.7 m height values.
In system/controlDict, set application to interFoam, not twoPhaseEulerFoam, because the task requires a Volume-of-Fluid sharp-interface solver rather than an Eulerian two-phase slip model.
In system/controlDict, set endTime to 1.0 s, deltaT to 0.001 s, adjustTimeStep to yes, maxCo to 0.5, and maxAlphaCo to 0.5.
In system/controlDict, set writeInterval to 0.1 s, producing ten output frames over the one-second simulation.
In system/controlDict, set writeFormat to ASCII, writePrecision to 8, and purgeWrite to 0 so that all ten frames are retained on disk with full precision.
Place all time-stepping parameters (deltaT, adjustTimeStep, maxCo, maxAlphaCo, endTime, writeInterval, writeFormat, writePrecision, purgeWrite) in the same system/controlDict file alongside the application line.
All geometric dimensions and initialization parameters are derived from the Martin and McCowan 1982 benchmark and correspond to the standard OpenFOAM tutorial tutorials/multiphase/interFoam/ras/damBreak.
